printed_marks.location: corners of the thin black frame enclosing the patch array and its printed row/column labels; a white L-bracket sits just inside each

fiducials.notes: Place the target by the four corners of the black frame -- the vertex where its horizontal and vertical rules meet, which is a crisp line intersection rather than a rounded patch corner. Order is the TARGET's, clockwise from the corner nearest patch A1. The frame encloses the printed row and column labels as well as the patches, so the patch array is inset from it.

patch_grid.coordinate_frame: Relative to the quadrilateral formed by the four black frame corners.

measured_from.method: perspective-rectified capture of a physical unit; grid optimised for agreement with the unit's own CxF reference
measured_from.unit: LaserSoft ISO 12641-2 advanced target, serial T1910021, Fuji Provia 100F
measured_from.notes: Patches butt directly together on this target, with no gaps, so gradient projection cannot find every boundary -- an edge only appears where adjacent patches differ. Autocorrelation fixed the pitch and the origin was then optimised against the reference. A mean of 0.836 dE2000 across all 864 patches is only achievable if the grid and the patch-id mapping are both right.

patch_grid.notes: 24 rows (A-X) x 36 columns (1-36) = 864 patches. Patch id is {row_letter}{column_number}, e.g. 'X36' -- the opposite convention to the ColorChecker SG, confirmed against the unit's CxF file.

reference_data.notes: LaserSoft publish a per-unit CxF3 measurement keyed by the barcode printed on the target. The file's Serial tag carries the same value, so it pairs automatically once it is in a reference library.

patches.notes: Neutral scale step 1 (lightest, L* ~88.0). The scale runs serpentine across columns 31-34: column 31 descends A->X, 32 ascends, 33 descends, 34 ascends, and the four interlock into one continuous 96-step ramp. Membership and order were both derived from the measured reference, and order is re-derived at analysis time so a differently laid-out unit is reported rather than mis-plotted.

tonal_response.notes: 96 neutral steps across columns 31-34, L* ~1.6 to ~88.

notes:
Transmissive target: measured in Colorimetric_Transmittance on Fuji Provia Professional film. The applicable FADGI category is Photographic Transparencies, NOT Prints and Photographs -- and FADGI specifies no color accuracy metric for transparencies at all, because film is not scene referred. Delta E against this target's own reference is still a useful measurement and runs from a custom profile, but it is not a FADGI conformance criterion.
lightness_uniformity is deliberately NOT declared: the only repeated near-white patches are the highlight ends of six adjacent color ramps in rows A-B, clustered in one corner rather than distributed across the chart, which is not a usable areal-coverage uniformity sample.
No dimensional reference is printed on this target, so it cannot establish sampling frequency. That is a property of the target, not of any capture made with it.

ITS GAMUT EXCEEDS COMMON WORKING SPACES, AND THAT SHOWS UP AS CLIPPING RATHER THAN AS AN ERROR. On the sample capture -- 16-bit, tagged eciRGB v2 -- 127 of the 864 patches have at least one channel held at exactly the encoding floor. They are not underexposed and the placement is not wrong: they are the chart's saturated cyans, magentas and yellows, with ROI means as high as 0.60 and a single channel pinned at zero (33 red, 46 green, 46 blue, 2 both). Their median measured chroma is C*ab 57 against 23 for the other 737.

A truncated channel means the encoded colour is WRONG IN A KNOWN DIRECTION -- chroma understated, hue pulled toward the surviving primaries -- so Delta E against those patches measures the encoding rather than the capture. The engine flags them `gamut_clipped` and names the channel, and the colour metrics say so and include them anyway rather than silently shrinking the patch set.

THE REMEDY IS THE WORKING SPACE, NOT THE EXPOSURE. Capture this target into a space wide enough to hold it -- ProPhoto RGB rather than eciRGB v2 or Adobe RGB -- or accept that its most saturated patches cannot be judged. This is a property of the chart, which is an ISO 12641-2 ADVANCED target and is built with an extended gamut on purpose; it is not a fault of any particular capture, and it is worth knowing BEFORE shooting rather than after.

ONE DEFINITION SERVES EVERY FORMAT AND BOTH EDITIONS THAT HAVE BEEN CHECKED. LaserSoft image one design onto film and cut it to format, so the 4x5 and the 120 are the same chart at two scales, and nothing in this definition depends on scale -- it states no physical size. Checked on a 120 (6x6) unit, serial T1710030, which prints 'ISO 12641-2 Candidate 2017:10' where the 4x5 prints 'advanced target 2019:10': placed automatically by its printed frame, every one of the 864 ROIs inside its patch, worst inset sensitivity 0.0076 against a 0.02 limit. That is why the display name says neither 'Advanced' nor a format. What differs between units -- format, edition, film batch -- is carried by the per-unit CxF, keyed by the serial, which is the only place it can be told apart and the only place it matters.

THE BARCODE ENCODES THE SERIAL RATHER THAN SPELLING IT. T1910021 carries 1930021 and T1710030 carries 1730030: the product letter becomes a digit, the decade is dropped and twenty is added to the month, the same rule LaserSoft's IT8 charts follow. The reference bank applies the rule forward from each file's serial, so a unit's CxF pairs with its capture without a binding (reference/library.py, lasersoft_barcode).

dimensional_reference.notes: This target prints no scale, ruler or dimensioned feature, so nothing in a capture establishes its physical size. Deltachrome deliberately does NOT carry a figure measured from one specimen: the frame is imaged onto film that is then cut to format, and neither the imaging scale across production batches nor the placement of the cut is guaranteed, so a value from one unit would be an assumption about every other. Sampling frequency therefore reports N/A, which is what this declaration means: the resolution requirement still applies to the capture, it simply cannot be verified from this target. Use a target that carries dimensional markers, or measure a specific specimen and pass --fiducial-extent for that unit's captures only.
